Data/systems: for each steered generation, score property gain by (i) the naive predictor and (ii) a PROVENANCE-CONTROLLED oracle -- a predictor trained on a provenance-balanced/decorrelated split and/or an independent physics evaluator (FoldX/Rosetta-style stability; a second empirical logP model) that ignores provenance. Decisive metric (primary): SPURIOUS GAIN = naive-minus-controlled property-gain gap, as a fraction of the naive gain. Convincing positive: spurious gain >= 40% of naive gain (median, CI excludes 0) and correlated with the provenance-displacement fraction from Experiment 1 (Spearman rho>=0.5). Decision band: spurious gain in [15%, 40%) means part of the gain is real physics -- reported as a partial shortcut. Negative: spurious gain < 15% (controlled oracle largely confirms the naive gain) refutes H2 -- the gain reflects physics, and the shortcut account is withdrawn for that property.

Experiment 3 (H2/H3 -- The shortcut predicts designer-relevant failure). Tests that high-shortcut steering yields provenance-collapsed, low-novelty designs. Data/systems: per steered generation compute a provenance-shortcut score (share of gain attributable to provenance movement) and measure provenance clustering (collapse toward one organism/family/scaffold group in embedding space), novelty (identity/Tanimoto to nearest training object), and set diversity; regress these on the shortcut score. Decisive metric: Spearman rho / R^2 between shortcut score and provenance-collapse and novelty-loss. Convincing positive: rho >= 0.5 (CI excludes 0) for both collapse and novelty-loss -- the shortcut is a usable predictor of degenerate design. Decision band: rho in [0.3, 0.5) is a weak predictor -- reported with its error. Negative: rho <= 0.3 means the shortcut score does not forecast design degeneration, so its practical value is limited even if H1/H2 hold.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Provenance-invariant steering fixes it; positive control validates the pipeline). Tests that orthogonalizing the steering direction against provenance features preserves genuine (controlled-oracle) gain while restoring novelty and reducing collapse, and that the whole detection/fix pipeline recovers a known planted shortcut. Data/systems: (a) construct a debiased direction by projecting the property direction off the provenance subspace (Gram-Schmidt), compare provenance-invariant vs standard steering at matched displacement on controlled-oracle gain, provenance-collapse, novelty, validity; (b) POSITIVE CONTROL -- relabel a subset so a property artificially co-occurs with a tag, confirm the pipeline recovers the planted shortcut and the fix removes it. Decisive metrics: change in controlled-oracle gain and in novelty/collapse from invariant vs standard steering; and planted-shortcut recovery rate in the positive control. Convincing positive: invariant steering retains >= 80% of the controlled-oracle gain while cutting provenance-collapse by >= 30% and restoring novelty toward the unsteered baseline, AND the positive control recovers the planted shortcut (detection AUROC>=0.9) with the fix removing it. Decision band: controlled-gain retention in [60%, 80%) or collapse reduction in [10%, 30%) means the fix trades some genuine signal for debiasing -- reported as a quantified trade. Negative: invariant steering destroys controlled-oracle gain (retention < 60%) means physics and provenance are inseparable for that property (reported per property), or a failed positive control invalidates the pipeline and is reported before any real-data claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Provenance-controlled oracles and physics evaluators (FoldX/Rosetta, second logP model) are in-silico proxies; the core claim rests on DISAGREEMENT between a naive predictor and a provenance-decorrelated one, plus displacement into a provenance feature subspace—stated explicitly, not as wet-lab truth. 2) Physics and provenance may be irreducibly entangled for some properties (family IS the mechanism); we handle this by reporting the entanglement per property and restricting strong claims to properties where a provenance-orthogonal physics direction demonstrably exists (validated by the controlled oracle). 3) The debiasing fix could remove genuine signal if physics and provenance share a subspace; we quantify the tradeoff via the controlled oracle rather than assume a free lunch. 4) SAE quality/layer choice could produce spurious 'provenance features'; controlled with multiple SAE variants, difference-of-means baselines, random-direction controls, and the synthetic positive control (experiment 6). 5) If standard steering turns out NOT to ride provenance (gains survive the controlled oracle), that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable-feature steering targets physics, not database artifacts. 6) In-silico property/validity metrics limit conclusions to model-internal design behavior, not experimental function.

Name: steering_sideeffect_law
Title: The Conservation of Trouble: Are Off-Target Property Drifts of Interpretable-Feature Steering Lawful and Predictable in Scientific Generative Models?
Short Hypothesis: When an interpretable feature is steered to control one property of a generated protein or molecule, it induces off-target drift in OTHER, structurally-verifiable properties that is not random noise but LAWFUL: the drift vector across all properties is predicted, before any generation, by a fixed feature-specific 'side-effect signature' derived from the geometry of the SAE dictionary. This lets practitioners forecast and pre-empt collateral damage, choosing minimal-side-effect features and orthogonalized directions to hit a target property while holding others fixed.
Related Work: Text-LLM steering studies extensively document off-target side effects and entanglement: SAE-Targeted Steering (Chalnev et al. 2024) minimizes side effects using SAE-measured effect vectors; Rogue Scalpel (2025), Steering Externalities (2026), SteeringSafety (2025), Steering Refusal with SAEs (2024), and Mind the Performance Gap (2026) all show steering degrades unrelated capabilities or safety in a method/model-dependent way. Crucially, all of these (a) operate in TEXT LLMs where the off-target 'property' is a fuzzy behavior or benchmark score, and (b) treat side effects as a nuisance to be measured post hoc or empirically minimized. Scientific-model steering work (InterPLM 2024, ProtSAE 2025, chemistry-LM SAEs) reports only ON-target property gains and evaluates validity as a side constraint, never characterizing structured off-target property drift. No prior work (i) transfers the off-target-drift phenomenon to scientific generative models where every off-target property (helix content, charge, logP, ring count, motif presence) is an OBJECTIVELY VERIFIABLE structural fact, (ii) tests whether the drift is LAWFUL and predictable a priori from a fixed feature side-effect signature rather than needing per-target measurement, or (iii) turns that law into a pre-flight side-effect forecaster and a minimal-collateral feature/direction selector. This distinguishes it from my prior compositionality proposal (which co-steers several INTENDED targets) by studying UNINTENDED drift on non-targeted properties and its a-priori predictability. DELTA vs text-LLM pre-intervention side-effect prediction (Chalnev et al. 2024, SAE-Targeted Steering): they minimize side effects using effect vectors MEASURED empirically per target, whereas we predict the drift vector A PRIORI from fixed dictionary geometry (decoder overlaps + property-Jacobian) with NO generation, against HARD structural oracles. We claim a domain- and battery-specific empirical regularity, not a universal theory. Three separable contributions: (1) the finding (structured drift), (2) the predictor (geometry-derived signature), (3) the method (minimal-collateral controller); each is publishable on its own even if a later one fails.
Abstract: Steering an interpretable feature to control one property of a generated protein or molecule is the standard controllable-design paradigm, judged mainly by whether the target property moves. In text language models, steering is known to cause off-target effects, and SAE-based methods (e.g., Chalnev et al. 2024) minimize them using EMPIRICALLY-MEASURED effect vectors; but there the off-target 'property' is a fuzzy behavior and the effect must be measured per target. We make two moves. First, a new SETTING: in scientific generative models every off-target property (helix content, charge, logP, ring count, motif presence) is an objectively verifiable structural fact, so collateral drift becomes a measurable VECTOR, not a benchmark wobble. Second, a sharper QUESTION: can that drift be predicted a priori, before any generation, from the SAE dictionary geometry alone? We hypothesize each feature carries a fixed 'side-effect signature' -- computable from decoder-direction overlaps and a per-feature property-Jacobian -- that forecasts its drift vector. We frame this as a domain- and battery-specific empirical regularity, not a universal law. Using ESM-2 and a SMILES chemical LM with sparse autoencoders, we test three separable hypotheses: (1) single-target steering induces structured, non-random off-target drift under hard oracles; (2) the geometry-derived signature predicts each feature's measured drift vector, with a NO-SURROGATE decoder-overlap-only variant guarding against proxy leakage; and (3) the signature powers a pre-flight forecaster and a minimal-collateral controller (low-drift feature selection or orthogonalization) that hold non-target properties fixed, quantifying compute saved versus generation-based screening. Users and workflows: protein design, molecular optimization, and multi-property/constraint-satisfaction generative design, plus model evaluation and safety auditing of steered outputs.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Property battery, each with a cheap HARD oracle so drift is objective: proteins -- alpha-helix fraction, beta-sheet fraction, GRAVY, net charge, molecular weight, motif presence (HMMER/regex); molecules -- logP, QED, ring/aromatic-ring count, molecular weight, TPSA, functional-group SMARTS. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). Feature bank: ~30-50 property-linked target features per domain (probe AUROC>=0.8 on 2,000 held-out natural objects) plus difference-of-means directions. Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; norm-matched random-direction controls throughout; 500 generations per feature x strength level. SCOPE: the side-effect signature is computed PER FEATURE and predicts a drift VECTOR over the full property battery; we test whether it holds per model size, per SAE variant, and per domain, and report where it fails rather than asserting universality. All decisive thresholds below are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals over seeds.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Single-target steering induces structured, non-random off-target drift). Tests that steering one property drifts other properties in a consistent, non-noise direction. Data/systems: for each target feature, sweep steering strength {0.1...1.0}; at each level measure the FULL property vector; the off-target drift vector = change in every non-target property; compare against a norm-matched random direction. Decisive metrics: (a) collateral magnitude = off-target drift norm relative to on-target gain; (b) DIRECTION CONSISTENCY = mean cosine of the drift vector across seeds and adjacent strengths; (c) correlation of output-side checks (validity/pseudo-perplexity/RDKit-validity) with true off-target drift. Convincing positive: direction consistency >= 0.7 (drift is a stable signature, well above the random-direction control's ~0) AND output-side-vs-drift correlation in [-0.2, 0.2] (standard evals are blind to it). Decision band: consistency in [0.4, 0.7) means drift is partly structured, partly noise -- reported as such; output-side correlation with |r| in (0.2, 0.4] means checks catch some drift, tempering the blind-spot claim. Negative: consistency < 0.4 (drift is essentially random across seeds) refutes H1's "lawful" premise -- a clean negative result warning against a-priori side-effect claims.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- A geometry-derived side-effect signature predicts the drift vector). Tests that an intervention-free signature computed from the SAE dictionary forecasts each feature's measured drift vector. Data/model: per feature compute (i) decoder-direction overlaps -- cosine of the feature's decoder direction with other property features' directions; (ii) a per-feature property-Jacobian -- gradient of each differentiable-surrogate property predictor w.r.t. residual-stream activations projected onto the feature direction. Predict the drift vector from these; correlate with the measured drift vector from Experiment 1; baselines -- concept-correlation and a chance permutation. Decisive metric (primary): cosine similarity / R^2 between predicted and actual drift vectors across features, plus per-property Spearman. Convincing positive: predicted-vs-actual drift cosine >= 0.6 (bootstrap CI excludes the concept-correlation baseline and chance) -- establishing lawfulness. Decision band: cosine in [0.35, 0.6) means the signature captures the dominant coupling but misses structure -- reported as partial law, usable for ranking not exact forecasting. Negative: cosine <= 0.35 (no better than concept-correlation/chance) means the drift is not predictable from dictionary geometry, refuting H2 (H1 may still hold descriptively).

Experiment 3 (H3 -- Pre-flight forecaster ranks features by collateral before generation). Tests that the signature ranks features by expected total collateral without any generation. Data/systems: use the signature to rank all target features by forecast total collateral for each target property; validate against the measured collateral from Experiment 1. Decisive metric: precision@k for selecting genuinely low-collateral features, and rank correlation (Spearman) between forecast and measured collateral. Convincing positive: precision@5 >= 0.8 and Spearman >= 0.6 (CI excludes 0), with quantified compute saved vs generation-based screening, plus a human-readable forecast per feature. Decision band: precision@5 in [0.6, 0.8) or Spearman in [0.4, 0.6) means the forecaster is a useful but imperfect screen -- reported with its error rate. Negative: precision@5 <= 0.6 means the ranking is not actionable, and the forecasting payoff is withdrawn.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Minimal-collateral controller hits target while holding others fixed; positive control). Tests that selecting low-forecast-collateral features or orthogonalizing against held-fixed property axes Pareto-dominates naive steering. Data/systems: (a) select lowest-forecast-collateral feature for the target; (b) orthogonalize the steering direction against the property-Jacobian axes of properties to be held fixed; compare to naive best-concept-correlation steering on on-target gain, off-target drift on held-fixed properties, validity, novelty. POSITIVE CONTROL: two features constructed to share a decoder subspace (high overlap) and two known-orthogonal ones -- confirm the signature predicts high vs low cross-property drift. Decisive metric (primary): area of the target-gain-vs-collateral Pareto frontier, and held-fixed drift reduction at matched on-target gain. Convincing positive: orthogonalized/selected steering cuts held-fixed drift by >= 30% at matched on-target gain (Pareto-dominates naive), AND the positive control shows high-overlap pairs drift >= 3x more than orthogonal pairs. Decision band: held-fixed drift reduction in [10%, 30%), or on-target gain lost to achieve it, is a quantified trade rather than domination -- reported as such. Negative: no frontier improvement over naive steering (< 10% drift reduction), or a failed positive control, means the controller offers no practical collateral control and the applied claim fails.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico property oracles (ESMFold/DSSP, RDKit/SMARTS, biopython) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal, structurally-defined off-target drift and its predictability, not experimental function. 2) The property-Jacobian requires a differentiable surrogate for properties measured by non-differentiable evaluators (HMMER motifs, folding); we quantify surrogate fidelity and also report the purely-geometric decoder-overlap predictor which needs no surrogate. 3) Off-target drift could be dominated by generic validity collapse rather than structured coupling; we isolate the regime where objects stay valid and report structured drift separately, using random-direction controls. 4) The law may be property-pair- or model-specific rather than universal; we test multiple properties, model sizes, and SAE variants and report where it fails—a negative/conditional result is still informative. 5) The orthogonalization fix may reduce on-target gain or interpretability; we quantify the tradeoff on the frontier rather than assume a free lunch. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both drift and signature; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, difference-of-means baselines, and the positive control. 7) If drift turns out to be unpredictable noise, that is a clean, publishable negative result constraining theories of feature-dictionary geometry and warning against a-priori side-effect claims.

Name: chirality_syntactic_shortcut
Title: A Tag, Not a Concept: Do String-Based Molecular Generators Represent Chirality Causally or Copy It as Syntax?
Short Hypothesis: String-based (SMILES/SELFIES) molecular generative models emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) not because they possess a semantically-grounded internal representation of 3D chirality, but as a largely syntactic copy-from-context habit. We hypothesize that (i) NO compact intervention was FOUND -- under multiple intervention types, layers, and strengths -- that causally flips a stereocenter's configuration while holding the rest of the molecule fixed; (ii) instead, the model tracks a shallow 'stereo-parity bookkeeping' signal tied to local ring/branch syntax; and (iii) this makes controlled enantiomer design (asking for the R vs S form of a specified scaffold) systematically unreliable in a way ordinary validity/property checks never reveal. We keep decodability, steerability, and design-reliability as three separately-tested claims, and confirm the intervention pipeline works on a known non-chiral feature before reading any null on chirality.
Related Work: Chirality is known to break geometric ML: 'E(3)-equivariant models cannot learn chirality' (2024) proves 3D-invariant GNNs discard it, and chirality-aware GNNs (MolKGNN 2023, ChiENN 2023, tetrahedral MPNNs 2020, ChiDeK 2026) add architecture to recover it. On the generative side, 'Stereochemistry-aware string-based molecular generation' (2025) shows string models CAN emit stereochemistry but says nothing about the internal mechanism. Mechanistic work on molecular transformers ('Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' 2025) finds ring/branch syntax circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and SynFlowNet interpretability (2025) finds decodable physicochemical features - but NEITHER examines chirality, the one property where 2D connectivity is uninformative and a genuine internal 3D concept would be required. No prior interpretability study asks whether a string-based generator's stereochemistry tokens are backed by a causal, steerable chirality representation or are a syntactic shortcut, nor audits controlled-enantiomer design reliability through this lens. This distinguishes the proposal from all prior chirality-architecture work (which changes the model) and from my own prior steering proposals (which assumed the target property has a genuine internal handle). Here the central claim is the ABSENCE of such a handle for the hardest, most safety-critical property. DELTA vs 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025): that work analyzes attention/residual-stream circuits correlationally and never intervenes on stereochemistry; our causal edit test can FALSIFY a chirality representation by showing an intervention cannot flip a stereocenter while holding the graph fixed -- something correlational analyses cannot establish. This is a new causal test, not a claim that chirality has never been studied. Three separable claims -- decodability, steerability, design-reliability -- each with its own acceptance criterion; a positive control on a known non-chiral steerable feature guards against a weak-pipeline artifact.
Abstract: Chirality determines whether a drug heals or harms -- enantiomers share identical 2D connectivity yet can differ drastically in safety and potency -- and it is the one molecular property that cannot be read off a graph, requiring genuine 3D reasoning. String-based generative models (SMILES/SELFIES language models) routinely emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) and pass validity checks, but whether they hold an internal, causally-manipulable representation of chirality or merely copy stereo tags as local syntax is unknown. Prior mechanistic work on molecular transformers analyzes attention and residual-stream circuits for ring/branch syntax and valence, but never causally intervenes on stereochemistry; our delta is a causal edit test that can FALSIFY a chirality representation -- showing an intervention cannot flip a stereocenter while holding the graph fixed -- which correlational attention/probe analyses cannot. Training sparse autoencoders on SMILES/SELFIES language models, we separate three claims: (1) DECODABILITY -- probe stereocenter configuration, net of a purely syntactic control probe; (2) STEERABILITY -- whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter (R->S) in the finished molecule while holding the rest of the graph, other centers, and validity fixed, with a POSITIVE CONTROL steering a known non-chiral feature (valence capacity) to prove the pipeline can steer; and (3) INTERPRETATION plus a DESIGN-RELIABILITY AUDIT -- whether located units track true CIP parity or shallow syntax, and how often requesting a specified enantiomer silently returns the wrong one, undetected by validity/likelihood. We predict no clean causal chirality handle, stereo tokens riding syntax, and silent enantiocontrol failure -- yielding a concrete pre-flight enantioreliability check, for medicinal chemists and generative-model builders, for when generated stereochemistry can be trusted. A positive (steerable handle) result is equally actionable, enabling controllable stereochemical generation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: autoregressive SMILES and SELFIES language models (~90M parameters), trained by us (or public checkpoints where available) on a stereochemistry-rich subset of ChEMBL/PubChem that retains @/@@ and E/Z tags (~2M molecules with defined stereocenters); two model sizes (~30M, ~90M) for scaling. Base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) on mid-layer residual streams (two layers), seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Ground truth via RDKit: canonical CIP labels (R/S) per stereocenter, E/Z per double bond, enantiomer/diastereomer relations. Validity gates: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid, stereochemically well-defined (no undefined-but-implied centers). Interventions: SAE-feature clamp/steer, difference-of-means (R-minus-S) direction, and enantiomer activation-patching; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; strength swept.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline that stereochemistry is genuinely emitted, then: is chirality decodable?). Establishes that the model emits correct, non-trivial stereochemistry (so a later null steering result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact), and locates candidate chirality directions. Data: 5,000 generated valid molecules with defined stereocenters; 2,000 held-out natural molecules for probing. Baseline metric: fraction of generated stereocenters whose CIP label matches a chemically sensible completion and stereo-token accuracy vs a copy-context null. Probing: at token positions surrounding each stereocenter, train linear/MLP probes to predict CIP R/S from residual activations and from SAE features; report AUROC vs generation-progress and layer, against an SAE-independent raw-activation probe AND against a purely syntactic control probe (predict whether the next stereo token is @ vs @@ from the partial string). Decisive metric: chirality-probe AUROC minus syntax-probe AUROC. Convincing baseline+location: model stereo-token accuracy clearly above the copy-context null AND chirality-probe AUROC>=0.75. Decision band: chirality-minus-syntax AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the "chirality" decodability is largely syntax prediction -- flagged, and location is treated as syntactic. Negative baseline: if the model does not emit correct stereochemistry above the copy null, the study is under-powered for absence claims and reported as inconclusive rather than confirming H1.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- No compact causal stereocenter-flip handle). Tests whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter R->S while holding the rest of the graph, other centers, and validity fixed. Data: 3,000 single-stereocenter molecules and 1,500 multi-stereocenter molecules. Systems: SAE-feature intervention, difference-of-means direction, and enantiomer activation-patching, each vs random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; dose-response swept. PIPELINE POSITIVE CONTROL: on the same molecules we steer a known NON-CHIRAL feature (valence capacity, per prior molecular-transformer mechanistic work) and require it to change the intended structural property above the random control, proving the intervention pipeline can steer before any null on chirality is interpreted as absence. Decisive metric (primary): ENANTIOFLIP SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions producing the exact mirror configuration at the TARGET center while (a) keeping the 2D graph identical, (b) leaving other centers unchanged, (c) preserving validity. Convincing support for H1 (no handle): best-intervention enantioflip success <= 15% (barely above the random-direction control) despite the confirmed baseline, with failures dominated by graph corruption / wrong-center flips / racemization. Decision band: success in (15%, 40%] is a PARTIAL/UNRELIABLE handle -- reported as neither clean absence nor clean presence; center-specificity (multi-center bleed rate) decides how it is framed. Negative (refutes H1): success >= 40% with high specificity means a genuine steerable chirality handle EXISTS -- an equally publishable positive finding that overturns the hypothesis.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- The signal is shallow syntactic parity bookkeeping, not 3D parity). Tests whether the located units track true CIP parity or local @/@@ ring/branch syntax. Data: controlled substrate pairs -- (i) molecules where the same @/@@ token maps to opposite CIP labels depending on neighbor ordering, and (ii) matched pairs where CIP label is constant but ring/branch context varies; plus SMILES-rewriting/canonicalization that preserves the molecule (random non-canonical SMILES re-enumeration via RDKit with fixed atom mapping, so the molecule and its CIP labels are provably unchanged while token order and ring-closure syntax vary). Decisive metric: feature-meaning INVARIANCE under molecule-preserving SMILES rewriting = correlation of feature activation with true CIP parity vs with raw @/@@ syntax. Convincing support for H2: feature tracks raw syntax (syntax correlation >= 0.7) and flips meaning under rewriting (CIP-parity correlation <= 0.3). Decision band: mixed loadings (both correlations in [0.3, 0.7)) means the unit is partly conceptual, partly syntactic -- reported as intermediate, not a clean shortcut. Negative: feature stays invariant to rewriting and tracks true CIP parity (parity correlation >= 0.7) means the model has a genuine 3D-parity representation, refuting H2.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Controlled-enantiomer design is silently unreliable, missed by output-side checks). Tests that requesting a specified enantiomer often returns the wrong one and that validity/likelihood do not detect it while an internal probe does. Data: request a SPECIFIED enantiomer of given scaffolds, stratified by number of stereocenters and scaffold complexity; 3,000 requests. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT ENANTIO-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid outputs returning the wrong enantiomer, opposite/undefined configuration, racemate, or chirality at a different center; secondary: detection AUROC/calibration of output-side signals (RDKit-validity, likelihood/perplexity, a property-predictor's confidence) vs the internal chirality-probe score from Experiment 1 for catching wrong-enantiomer outputs. Convincing positive: silent enantio-error rate rising with stereocenter count to >= 30% at >=2 centers, with output-side detection AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance) while the internal probe reaches AUROC>=0.75 -- a usable pre-flight enantioreliability filter. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means unreliability is present but modest; internal-probe AUROC in [0.6, 0.75) is a weak filter -- reported with its error. Negative: error rate < 15% and output-side signals already detect errors (AUROC>=0.7) means enantiocontrol is reliable / already checkable, refuting H3. Robustness across SMILES vs SELFIES, two model sizes, two SAE variants, and E/Z stereochemistry; test whether enantioflip success or error rate improves with scale or training stereochemistry density.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal handle), which requires strong effort to steer before concluding failure; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, enantiomer activation-patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the baseline in step 1 to confirm the model does emit correct stereochemistry - so a null enantioflip is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. 2) A positive result (a genuine steerable chirality handle exists) is equally publishable and would itself be a novel, useful finding for stereocontrolled design. 3) Stereochemistry ground truth relies on RDKit CIP assignment, which can be ambiguous for exotic centers; we restrict to well-defined central and E/Z stereochemistry and report assignment confidence. 4) Claims concern model-internal representation and string-level stereochemistry, not wet-lab bioactivity; the safety framing is about reliably producing the REQUESTED enantiomer, an objective structural fact. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) SMILES/SELFIES tokenization differences may complicate cross-encoding comparison; we standardize the stereochemistry evaluation on RDKit-parsed finished molecules. 7) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability (syntactic-vs-conceptual diagnosis) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly.

Name: symmetry_shortcut_crystal
Title: Symmetry Without Understanding? Auditing Whether Crystal Generative Models Causally Represent Space-Group Constraints or Silently Fake Them
Short Hypothesis: Crystal generative models conditioned on a target space group satisfy the constraint not because they possess a compact, causally-manipulable internal representation of the requested symmetry, but via a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut. We hypothesize (i) there is a decodable but only weakly causally-steerable internal 'space-group' direction; (ii) steering it to request a NEW space group frequently yields structures whose achieved symmetry silently mismatches the request (wrong space group, lower symmetry, or broken periodicity) while still passing validity/stability checks; and (iii) an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency signal predicts these silent failures better than output-side likelihood or formation-energy proxies.
Related Work: Symmetry-aware crystal generation is a rich area: SymmCD (2025), DiffCSP++/Space-Group-Constrained Generation (2024), WyCryst (2023), and PGCGM (2022) either hard-code space-group/Wyckoff constraints or condition on them. Critically, Ishii et al. (2026, WyckoffDiff-Adaptor) show that conditional symmetry control 'may not be sufficiently effective when space group constraints are applied as a condition'—i.e., models silently violate the requested symmetry—but treat this as an architecture problem, not a representational one. Interpretability in materials (CGCNN 2018, Site-Net 2022, RankAAE 2023) is confined to PREDICTIVE property models with attention/latent-descriptor analysis; none examines the internal mechanism of GENERATIVE crystal models, and none asks whether symmetry—the defining, physics-critical property of crystals—is a genuine causal handle or a copying shortcut. No prior work (a) locates and causally tests a space-group representation inside a crystal generator, (b) shows symmetry-conditioned generation silently fakes the requested symmetry via a shortcut, or (c) provides an internal symmetry-reliability audit that catches these failures. This distinguishes the proposal from all symmetry-architecture work (which changes the model) and mirrors, in a new object class and for a new property (crystallographic symmetry vs stereochemistry), the shortcut-auditing lens of prior molecular proposals. CLOSEST-PRIOR-WORK CONTRAST: (i) known failure phenomenon -- Ishii et al. 2026 report silent symmetry violation but treat it as architecture; (ii) architecture fixes -- SymmCD/DiffCSP++/WyCryst hard-code or condition symmetry; (iii) predictive-model interpretability -- CGCNN/Site-Net/RankAAE analyze property predictors, not generators; (iv) molecular shortcut-auditing -- our prior lens, here transferred to crystallographic symmetry. Setting-specific difference: crystal symmetry is a discrete, globally-defined group constraint (not a local per-token property), invariant to equivalent cell/origin re-descriptions -- so a genuine representation must be re-description-invariant, a test with no molecular analogue. Novelty is the mechanistic explanation plus a released, model-agnostic audit artifact, not the mismatch itself.
Abstract: Symmetry is the defining property of a crystal: its space group dictates physical behavior and is the primary control knob in crystal generative models, which hard-code it or condition on it. Recent work shows conditional symmetry control can silently fail -- models emit structures lacking the requested space group. Our novelty is NOT rediscovering that mismatch but explaining it mechanistically and converting the explanation into a reusable audit. We ask: do crystal generators possess an internal, causally-manipulable representation of the requested symmetry, or satisfy the constraint through a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut? Using open symmetry-conditioned diffusion generators (DiffCSP++/SymmCD-style) on Materials Project data, we (1) LOCATE candidate space-group representations by probing the denoiser's activations, controlling for trivial copying of the conditioning token; (2) CAUSALLY test whether a compact intervention converts generation from space group A to B -- yielding a structure whose ACHIEVED symmetry (pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer over a tolerance sweep) matches B while composition and atom count are held fixed -- the operational definition of a genuine handle, distinguished from a copied conditioning signal; (3) INTERPRET whether located units encode true symmetry (invariant to equivalent cell re-descriptions and origin choices) or surface lattice/Wyckoff statistics; and (4) AUDIT reliability via the SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE and an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency score benchmarked against likelihood, formation-energy proxies, and a simple output-side symmetry heuristic. We deliver a model-agnostic, plug-in-without-retraining symmetry-reliability audit suite plus a controlled re-description dataset, and propose a minimal reporting standard. Stakeholders: crystal-generation researchers and computational materials scientists screening generated candidates, where silent symmetry errors waste relaxation compute and corrupt downstream property assumptions.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: open symmetry-conditioned crystal diffusion generators with accessible per-step denoiser activations -- a coordinate-based diffusion (DiffCSP++-style) and a Wyckoff-based diffusion (SymmCD/WyckoffDiff-style) checkpoint, trained on Materials Project / MP-20. Base weights frozen; only probes/SAEs trained. Achieved-symmetry ground truth: pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer over a tolerance sweep (record achieved space group, crystal system, point group, Wyckoff multiplicities). Validity gates: bond-length/overlap checks, charge neutrality, StructureMatcher novelty; stability proxy = energy-above-hull from a pretrained universal ML interatomic potential (CHGNet/MACE-MP), NO DFT. Probes: linear/MLP on denoiser residual activations at multiple timesteps/layers; difference-of-means directions and full activation-patching for intervention; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-symmetry-feature controls. 500 generations per condition. DELIVERABLE: a released model-agnostic symmetry-consistency AUDIT SUITE (usable as a plug-in pre-flight filter on existing generators without retraining) and a CONTROLLED RE-DESCRIPTION dataset (structures paired with symmetry-preserving cell/origin re-descriptions). All match rates, AUROCs, and subgroup effects are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals over >=3 seeds and multiple-comparison control across space-group strata; numeric decision thresholds below are pre-registered, and where arbitrary we also report the corresponding relative comparison and CI. Per-step denoiser activations and activation patching are confirmed extractable for the named open checkpoints via forward hooks on the denoiser network.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline reproduction, then: is the space group decodable?). Establishes that the model unconditionally reproduces target space groups above chance (so absence/weak-steerability claims are meaningful) and that space group is decodable internally. Data: 5,000 conditioned generations spanning the space-group vocabulary; probes trained on denoiser activations. Baseline metric: requested-vs-achieved space-group match rate vs a frequency-matched random-request chance level. Decoding: probe accuracy for target space group, crystal system, and lattice class vs timestep/layer, against a control probe that predicts the raw conditioning-token embedding (to gauge trivial copy-of-condition). Decisive metric: symmetry-probe accuracy minus condition-copy-probe accuracy. Convincing baseline+decodability: baseline match rate clearly above chance AND space-group probe accuracy >= 0.7 that exceeds the condition-copy control by >= 0.1. Decision band: probe-minus-copy gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the decodable signal is largely a copy of the conditioning input -- flagged. Negative baseline: if the model does not reproduce target space groups above chance, the study is under-powered for the steerability claim and reported as inconclusive.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- The space-group direction is only WEAKLY causally steerable). Tests whether intervening on the decoded direction switches the achieved space group from A to B. Data/systems: generations conditioned on space group A; intervene via probe-derived direction, difference-of-means (B-minus-A), and full activation-patching from a B-conditioned run, vs random-direction and matched-non-symmetry controls; dose-response swept. Causal controls are strengthened: timestep-matched random patching, layer-matched non-symmetry directions, and A-vs-B runs sharing the same random seed so only the symmetry intervention differs; composition and atom count are held fixed throughout so 'space-group switching' is unambiguous. Decisive metric (primary): SYMMETRY-SWITCH SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions yielding a finished structure whose SpacegroupAnalyzer symmetry equals B while composition and validity/stability are preserved and the change is specific. Convincing support for H1 (decodable-but-weakly-steerable): switch success in (5%, 40%] -- clearly above the random control (weakly causal) yet far below the conditioning baseline's match rate -- with failures skewed to subgroups of A/B. Decision band: success <= 5% means essentially NO causal handle (stronger than "weak"); >= 40% with specificity means a GENUINE strong handle -- either extreme is reported as such rather than as the hypothesized weak-steerability. Negative for the phenomenon: a strong, specific handle (>=40%) refutes the shortcut framing and is an equally publishable positive finding.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- Silent symmetry mismatches that pass validity/stability). Tests that requesting a new space group frequently yields valid+stable structures whose achieved symmetry silently differs from the request. Data/systems: across the full space-group vocabulary (stratified by crystal system, symmetry order, and training frequency), request each space group; among VALID+stable outputs measure the mismatch. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid+stable outputs whose achieved space group differs from requested, decomposed into correct-crystal-system-but-wrong-group, dropped-to-subgroup, and fully-broken-symmetry, stratified by requested symmetry order and training frequency. Convincing positive: silent error rate rising with symmetry order to >= 30% for high-symmetry / low-frequency requests, tolerance-robust across the SpacegroupAnalyzer sweep. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means mismatch exists but is modest -- reported as such; error rate that flips sign of conclusion across tolerances is reported as tolerance-sensitive and excluded from strong claims. Negative: error rate < 15% (models reliably achieve the requested symmetry) refutes H2. Interpretation sub-test (supports H1/H2): controlled crystal pairs dissociating space group from surface descriptors (same group / different lattice params or origin; different groups / similar lattice params) test whether the located feature is invariant to equivalent cell re-descriptions (true symmetry) or tracks lattice-parameter/Wyckoff-token statistics (shortcut) -- a feature that changes meaning under symmetry-preserving re-description is scored as a shortcut.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Internal symmetry-consistency signal beats output-side proxies at flagging silent failures). Tests that an intervention-free internal signal predicts silent symmetry errors better than likelihood or formation-energy proxies. Data/systems: for each generation compute an internal symmetry-consistency score (probe confidence / feature coherence read mid-generation); baselines -- generation likelihood, e-above-hull/formation-energy proxy, validity checks, a SIMPLE OUTPUT-SIDE SYMMETRY HEURISTIC (estimating symmetry from the partial/finished structure directly, no internals), and a black-box raw-activation probe; target label = silent symmetry error from Experiment 3. Decisive metric (primary): detection AUROC and calibration ECE for flagging silent symmetry errors. Convincing positive: internal-signal AUROC >= 0.80 with ECE<=0.10 while output-side likelihood/energy proxies stay in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance), with quantified compute saved by aborting untrustworthy requests before full generation + relaxation. Decision band: internal AUROC in [0.65, 0.80), or its edge over the black-box probe in [0.03, 0.10) AUROC, means the internal signal works but its advantage over cheaper signals is marginal -- the interpretability (shortcut-vs-concept) diagnosis is then the contribution. Negative: output-side proxies already reach AUROC>=0.70, or the internal signal fails to beat them, refutes H3. Robustness across the two generator architectures, two tolerances, and high- vs low-symmetry groups.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal symmetry handle); we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (probe direction, difference-of-means, full activation patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the step-1 baseline to confirm the model does reproduce target space groups—so a null switch result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable symmetry handle) is equally publishable and useful for symmetry-controlled design. 2) Achieved-symmetry ground truth depends on SpacegroupAnalyzer tolerance; we sweep tolerances and report sensitivity, restricting strong claims to tolerance-robust cases. 3) Stability is assessed by ML interatomic potentials (CHGNet/MACE), an in-silico proxy for DFT/synthesizability; claims concern requested-vs-achieved symmetry (an objective crystallographic fact) and model-internal representation, not experimental synthesizability. 4) Requires generators with accessible per-step activations; scope limited to open, instrumentable models. 5) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (shortcut vs concept) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly. 6) Symmetry and lattice statistics may be irreducibly entangled for some space groups; the controlled re-description pairs (step 4) are designed to separate them and we report where separation is impossible.

Name: relational_feature_steering
Title: Intrinsic Is Easy, Relational Is Hard: Do Interpretable Features Give Causal Control Over a Protein's Binding Context, or Only Its Standalone Properties?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable features of protein language models afford causal, steerable control over a protein's INTRINSIC (partner-independent) properties (fold, hydrophobicity, motifs), but no comparably compact, causally-steerable feature is FOUND -- under an expanded search over layers, token positions, schedules, and multi-feature directions -- for RELATIONAL properties: the context-dependent fact that a designed protein binds a SPECIFIED partner. We define relational steerability operationally (an intervention must raise the intended-partner interface score MORE than the best decoy, i.e. specificity, not generic bindability). We hypothesize relational control is absent, entangled with intrinsic features, or requires partner-conditioned representations, so steering toward 'binds partner X' silently degrades to generic bindability -- an unrecognized blind spot in interpretability-guided binder design.
Related Work: All interpretability-for-generation work on protein language models—InterPLM (2024), ProtSAE (2025), Steering Protein Language Models/ASPO (2025), the antibody-SAE paper (2025), Automated Neuron Labelling (2025), and CB-pLM (2024)—discovers and steers features encoding INTRINSIC, single-protein properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger/binding-site motifs) and evaluates whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a large partner-aware PPI literature (BIPSPI 2018; D-SCRIPT 2021; ReCLIP 2026; partner-specific interface prediction 2011) establishes that binding is intrinsically RELATIONAL—the same residue's behavior depends on the partner—but this line is purely PREDICTIVE and never touches the internal features of a GENERATIVE model or their steerability. No prior work asks whether a protein generative model represents relational, partner-conditioned properties as causally-steerable features, contrasts the steerability of intrinsic vs relational properties, or exposes that binder-design steering toward a NAMED partner may collapse to generic bindability. This proposal is the first to introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation and to audit partner-specific controllability—distinct from all prior single-property steering and from all predictive PPI work. CONTRIBUTION BULLETS: (1) conceptual -- introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation; (2) methodological -- partner-conditioned probing/steering and an operational definition of relational steerability (specificity over the best decoy, not generic bindability); (3) empirical -- the intrinsic-easy/relational-hard asymmetry; (4) applied -- a reusable partner-specificity audit. Closest baselines contrasted: intrinsic single-property steering (assumes an internal handle exists), predictive partner-aware PPI models (never touch generator internals or steerability), and controllable binder-design methods (report bindability, not audited specificity). Scope is single-sequence PLMs specifically. The setting is not reducible to prior property steering because the label is UNDEFINED without a partner.
Abstract: Interpretability-guided protein design steers PLM features toward desired properties -- but every demonstrated property is INTRINSIC to a single protein (fold, hydrophobicity, a local motif). Real binder design demands RELATIONAL control: producing a protein that binds a SPECIFIED partner -- a fact meaningless without the partner and, from decades of PPI research, irreducibly context-dependent. We introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation (conceptual novelty) and a partner-conditioned probing/steering audit (methodological novelty), and give an operational definition of RELATIONAL STEERABILITY: an intervention is relationally steerable only if it raises the intended-partner interface score MORE than the best decoy (specificity), not merely generic bindability. We hypothesize an intrinsic-easy/relational-hard asymmetry: compact steerable features exist for intrinsic properties, but no compact steerable feature is FOUND -- under an expanded search over layers, token positions, schedules, and multi-feature directions -- for partner-specific binding, so steering toward 'binds partner X' silently collapses to promiscuity. Using ESM-2 and an antibody PLM (p-IgGen) with sparse autoencoders, we (1) confirm intrinsic control succeeds (pipeline calibration); (2) contrast intrinsic-vs-relational steerability and measure a promiscuity-collapse rate, controlling for generic confounds (interface propensity, hydrophobicity, charge, length, disorder, foldability, novelty); (3) test whether relational information is absent, entangled, or requires partner conditioning; and (4) audit how often steered binders silently bind the wrong/any partner while validity and generic-bindability pass, scored by ESMFold-in-complex with calibrated AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation. We frame impact as changing evaluation norms and delivering reusable specificity-audit panels for therapeutic-design, biologics-engineering, and benchmark-creation communities, not as validated binder design.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and an antibody PLM (p-IgGen), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32) and Ordered (for steerability) variants, dictionary 16384, on the residual stream at a layer chosen by an intrinsic-dimension heuristic, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. INTRINSIC-property oracles (cheap): alpha-helix/beta-sheet fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY, molecular weight, motifs (HMMER/regex). RELATIONAL oracle: binding to a SPECIFIED partner via in-silico complex prediction -- ESMFold-in-complex interface pLDDT/ipTM and interface contact count as a cheap first pass, AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a subset -- plus a SPECIFICITY panel of decoy partners (specificity = intended-partner score minus best-decoy score). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6, pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline. Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; SAE-feature, difference-of-means, partner-conditioned, random-direction, and matched-intrinsic-feature controls. To bound compute, partner panel = 20 targets, decoy panel = 10 per target, 300 steered designs per target. DATA/LABELS: partner panels and binder/non-binder labels are drawn from curated PPI datasets (experimentally-supported complexes and matched non-binders), split train/val/test with a <=30% inter-split sequence-identity cap (mmseqs2) and a 1:1 positive:negative balance; the 20 partners are held-out targets not used to fit any feature. INTERVENTION SEARCH (to justify any absence claim): before concluding no relational handle, we search multiple layers, token positions (including the prepended-partner region), steering schedules, and MULTI-FEATURE/compositional directions, not only single compact features. BASELINES beyond SAE features: supervised latent directions, activation patching from a bound-complex run, full-sequence partner-conditioned generation, and a retrieval/template control. CONFOUNDS regressed out or matched in all relational analyses: interface propensity, hydrophobicity, charge, length, disorder, foldability, and sequence novelty. RELATIONAL ORACLE: ESMFold-in-complex first pass with AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a calibrated subset (>=200 designs), with multiple interface scores (ipTM, interface pLDDT, contact count) reported alongside agreement/calibration analysis. All decision thresholds below are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Intrinsic properties are causally, specifically steerable). Tests that interpretable features give calibrated causal control over partner-independent properties, establishing the pipeline works. Data: intrinsic-property features located by probe AUROC>=0.8 on 2,000 held-out natural sequences. Systems: SAE-feature and difference-of-means steering vs random-direction control, strength swept. Decisive metric (primary): intrinsic property gain per unit budget within the validity gate, and effect specificity (target property moves, matched non-target intrinsic properties do not). Convincing positive: intrinsic property change >= 0.5 SD of the natural-sequence property distribution at a validity-preserving budget, clearly above the random-direction control, in >= 3 of 4 model x property settings -- confirming intrinsic control succeeds. Decision band: gain in [0.2, 0.5) SD means intrinsic control is weak in this pipeline -- reported as such, and it caps how strong the intrinsic-vs-relational contrast in Experiment 2 can be. Negative: no intrinsic feature steers its property above the random control means the pipeline lacks steering power, and no relational absence claim can be made (the study is reported as under-powered, not as confirming H2).

Experiment 2 (H2 -- No compact causally-steerable partner-specificity feature; relational collapses to generic bindability). Tests, in the SAME pipeline that just succeeded intrinsically, whether steering toward "binds partner X" yields intended-partner specificity or mere promiscuous bindability. Data/systems: relational features located both partner-agnostically and via partner-CONDITIONED activations (target partner prepended); steer toward each of the 20 partners via SAE-feature, difference-of-means (binders-of-X minus non-binders), and partner-conditioned directions, vs random and matched-intrinsic controls. Decisive metric (primary): the intrinsic-vs-relational STEERABILITY GAP -- relational specificity gain (intended-minus-best-decoy) per unit budget compared to the intrinsic gain from Experiment 1; and PROMISCUITY COLLAPSE RATE = fraction of steered binders whose binding score rises for intended AND decoy partners alike (zero specificity). Convincing support for H2: relational specificity gain <= 0.2x the intrinsic gain AND promiscuity collapse rate >= 60%, despite confirmed intrinsic control -- relational steering exists only as generic bindability. Decision band: relational-to-intrinsic gain ratio in (0.2, 0.5] or collapse rate in [40%, 60%) means relational control is weak-but-present -- reported as partial, not absent. Negative (refutes H2): relational specificity gain reaches >= 0.5x intrinsic gain with collapse rate < 40% means a genuine steerable partner-specific feature exists -- an equally publishable positive result.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- The relational signal is absent/entangled/partner-conditioned, not intrinsic specificity). Tests which of the three predicted regimes holds, using probing and interpretation. Data/systems: (a) partner-conditioned vs partner-agnostic probe AUROC for intended-partner binding -- does relational information exist without the partner in context? (b) controlled pairs -- same binder vs multiple partners, and different binders of the same partner -- to test whether located relational features encode partner-specificity or generic interface-propensity (a feature firing identically regardless of partner is generic); (c) a partner-conditioned architecture variant (partner prepended) to test whether relational steerability APPEARS when the partner is in context. Decisive metric: partner-conditioned minus partner-agnostic probe AUROC, and feature partner-invariance (activation correlation across partners). Convincing positive for "requires partner conditioning": partner-agnostic probe near chance (AUROC in [0.5, 0.6]) while partner-conditioned probe reaches >= 0.75, and relational steerability from Experiment 2 rises materially only in the partner-conditioned variant. Decision band: partner-conditioned advantage in [0.05, 0.15) AUROC means partner context helps only weakly -- the regime is reported as ambiguous between "absent" and "entangled". Negative: partner-agnostic probe already high AND features partner-specific means relational specificity is present intrinsically, refuting the entanglement/conditioning account.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Silent wrong-partner designs pass output-side checks; an internal probe flags them). Tests that steered binders bind the wrong/any partner while validity and generic-bindability checks pass, and that the internal specificity probe catches this. Data/systems: for the 20 target partners, request binders via steering; among valid, generically-bindable designs measure the failure and test detectors. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT WRONG-PARTNER RATE = fraction of valid, generically-bindable designs that bind a decoy at least as well as the intended partner; secondary: detection AUROC/ECE of output-side signals (validity, generic interface score, generation likelihood) vs the internal partner-conditioned specificity probe for catching wrong-partner designs. Convincing positive: silent wrong-partner rate >= 40% with output-side detection AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance) while the internal specificity probe reaches AUROC>=0.75 -- a usable pre-flight specificity filter, with quantified compute saved before expensive AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation. Decision band: wrong-partner rate in [20%, 40%) or internal-probe AUROC in [0.6, 0.75) means the blind spot is real but modest / the filter is weak -- reported with its error. Negative: wrong-partner rate < 20% and output-side checks already detect non-specific designs (AUROC>=0.7) means specificity is not a hidden blind spot, refuting H3's auditing claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The relational claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean steerable partner-specificity feature); we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, partner-conditioned steering), sweeping strength, and calibrating that intrinsic control DOES succeed in the same pipeline, so a null relational result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable partner-specific feature) is equally publishable and valuable for binder design. 2) Binding is scored by in-silico complex predictors (AlphaFold-Multimer/ESMFold interface metrics), which are proxies for wet-lab affinity/specificity; claims concern model-internal, in-silico-verified partner-specific controllability, not experimental binding—stated explicitly, and specificity uses relative (intended-vs-decoy) scores to reduce absolute-score bias. 3) Complex prediction is compute-heavier than single-sequence oracles; we cap partner and decoy panel sizes and use ESMFold-in-complex as a cheaper first-pass with AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a subset. 4) Relational information may simply be absent without the partner in context; the partner-conditioned probing/steering experiments are designed to detect exactly this and turn it into an informative finding about what representation relational control requires. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, difference-of-means baselines, and random-direction controls. 6) If relational steering unexpectedly succeeds with specificity, that overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive contribution. 7) We frame practical impact as changing evaluation norms and releasing reusable specificity-audit panels, not as validated binder design; wet-lab or stronger external validation is out of scope, and any design claim is in-silico only. We report what is learned under each outcome -- strong relational failure, weak relational control, or successful partner-specific steering -- so a null is informative rather than merely negative.
